description: Building a zigzag end paper so every leaf opens to the back and the structure yields to the drag of the cover. A folded sheet is marked and pasted up, folded back over the paste-down, and a further sheet inserted through which the sewing passes; a leather or cloth joint can be worked in at the same stage.
name: making end papers

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter V, p.82. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive

steps.description: Take a folded sheet a little larger than the book and mark two points an eighth of an inch from the back with dividers for the fold.
Paste the paste-down leaf up to the marked points and let the paste dry.
Fold the outer leaf back over the paste-down and turn the next leaf the reverse way to form the zigzag.
Insert a further folded sheet at the inner fold so the sewing can pass through it.
If joints are wanted, paste the edge of the thin leather or cloth into the fold and fold it over so the sewing catches both the joint and the inserted sheet.
After the book is pasted down, tear off the waste leaf and paste the remaining leaf down onto the board.
